title:
O, won’t we have a merry time,
 Drinking whisky, beer and wine!
 On coronation,
 Coronation day!
 O, won’t we have a merry time
 On coronation day!
html_source:
“Coronation Day” was a popular song at the turn of the century around the time of the coronation of King Edward VII. “Coronation Day” is also slang for “payday” since five shilling pieces were often referred to as crowns, so getting “coronated” was a slangy way of saying you were getting paid. The song’s words are repeated numerous times throughout the book. It is one of many ditties which Mulligan disrespectfully sings to refer to his current surroundings or situation in the book.
